subject: Extended Association Plots in R - troubleshooting

messages.author: c39625175da69e23
messages.subject: Extended Association Plots in R - troubleshooting
parts:
Hello, I am having trouble creating an extended association plot in R that shows there is a relationship between two variables. I'm using the assoc() function in the vcd package, using Rstudio (Version 0.97.551) through R (Version 3.0.1) on a Mac OS X 10.6.

My data is a 6x3 array with row and column names. Here's an example:

names<-c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E")
    y<-c(340, 37, 110, 17, 71)
    z<-c(720, 14, 6, 141, 120)
    x<-data.frame(names, y, z); x
The code I'm using is:

 x <- read.table(file.choose(), header=TRUE, row.names=1, sep="\t", comment.char=""); x # Load x.txt
    attach(x)
    x.m <- as.matrix(x[,]); x.m
    library(vcd)
    assocplot(t(x.m)) # Output regular association plot (residuals not shown) = normal plot.
    assoc(t(x.m)) # Output extended association plot with Pearson's residuals = error plot.

The regular assocplot() function calls a normal plot, with the associations in red and black tiles. Other vcd plots like mosaic all output fine. However, the assoc() function is calling an error plot that is just a bunch of letters centred on a very small location in the middle of the plot, with "A" and "B" labels on the x and y axis.

I have previously outputted an extended association plot with this data successfully, but as a relatively inexperienced R user, I'm not sure what the problem is now. I've tried various means of troubleshooting, including running the code in regular R as well as Rstudio (the problem persists), and many different forum searches. I've also asked other users to try the code above using my array. One successfully outputted an extended association plot on their machine (without shading), while two others outputted an error plot like mine (both using updated {vcd} packages). The latter two users have suggested there may be a bug, so I am going to contact the package authors, but I wanted to check if anyone is able to output from the assoc() or has recently experienced similar issues. Any suggestions would be appreciated.

With the following code, I get the same type of wrong plot:

# R 3.0.1 on Linux Mint 15 64bit KDE
# vcd 1.2-13
library(vcd); set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(floor(runif(18, 10,1000)), ncol=6,
dimnames=list(X=LETTERS[1:3], Y=letters[1:6]))
assoc(x)

Could indeed be a bug,
